div.head: Ps Cn for 13
div.ab: Si aduena uel peregrinus, qui de longinquo uenerit, sit calumniatus de foresta, et talis est sua inopia, ut non possit habere plegios, ad primam calumniam, quali nullus Anglus iudicari potest, tunc subeat captionem regis et ibi expectet, quousque uadat ad iudicium ferri et aque.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 622 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)
div.ab: If a stranger or foreigner who has come from afar is accused concerning the forest, and his poverty is such that he cannot have pledges, at the first accusation, in such a way as no Englishman can be judged [?], then let him undergo the king's arrest and wait there until he goes to the ordeal of iron and of water.

note.seg: die Worte sind nur äusserlich dem landrechtlichen Inhalt angeklebt, wie S. 620c
The words are only stuck on externally to the content taken from the general law, as on p. 620 note c

Ebd. Rückfall 1b. 10b (wo man Cn 55 in 35 bessere). Die vom Verf. eingeschmuggelten Wörter bedeuten einen Freiheitsanspruch im Prozess der von der Krone verklagten Untertanen, der wohl mit diesem Inhalte sonst nicht vorkommt, in der Form aber erinnert ans Programm der Magna charta 39: Nullus liber homo capiatur nisi per iudicium usw.

Ibid. Rückfall 1b. 10b (where Cn 55 should be corrected to 35). The words smuggled in by the author mean a claim to liberty in the trial of subjects sued by the Crown, which with this content probably does not occur elsewhere, but in its form recalls the programme of Magna Carta 39: Nullus liber homo capiatur nisi per iudicium etc.
